albumBackground: In January 1962, legendary German pianist Wilhelm Kempff entered Berlin's historical UFA-Tonstudio to record a monumental set of Mozart solo piano works for Deutsche Grammophon. Produced by Hans Weber with balance engineering by Heinz Wildhagen and supervision by executive producer Prof. Elsa Schiller, these sessions captured Kempff's distinctively poetic, singing tone and lucid phrasing on a Steinway Model D concert grand. While Kempff was best known for his authoritative Beethoven and Schubert interpretations, his Mozart playing brought an aristocratic grace, improvisatory freshness, and subtle dynamic shading that made these recordings timeless classics in the DGG catalog. Recorded during the golden age of Deutsche Grammophon's analogue stereo era, the production utilized custom valve mixing consoles and Neumann vacuum-tube microphones. The acoustics of the UFA-Tonstudio provided a rich natural reverberation that perfectly complemented Kempff's airy, unhurried touch and delicate pedaling. This Japanese pressing on Deutsche Grammophon (Catalog No: MGX7011, pressed in Japan by Polydor K.K.) is revered among classical vinyl collectors for its ultra-quiet virgin vinyl surface, pristine pressing quality, and master-tape fidelity. Japanese cutting engineers handled the tape transfer with meticulous care, maintaining the full dynamic range of the master tapes without applying peak limiting, allowing the delicate micro-dynamics and thunderous low-register chords to breathe naturally.
